questions.title: Collapse repeated delivery attempts
questions.prompt: Step 1 of 4. Implement collapse_attempts(attempts). Each attempt is a dictionary with string deliveryId and status values. Return one new dictionary with only deliveryId and status for each logical delivery. Return a fresh list. Keep the first attempt for a deliveryId and preserve the order in which distinct identifiers first appeared. Meet O(n) time and O(u) space for n attempts and u unique identifiers. When the function returns, the input list and its dictionaries must equal their original values.
constraints: attempts contains zero or more JSON-compatible dictionaries with string deliveryId and status values.
Return one new dictionary with deliveryId and status keys for each distinct deliveryId.
Return a fresh result list that does not reuse the input list.
The first occurrence wins and distinct identifiers retain first-seen order.
A duplicate may be non-adjacent; comparing only neighboring records is not sufficient.
Expected complexity: O(n) time and O(u) space for u unique delivery identifiers.
When the function returns, the input list and its dictionaries must equal their original values.

cases.label: rejects a non-adjacent duplicate without reordering

assertions.label: returns the first status for each identifier
keeps only the earliest x and y values

questions.title: Summarize an observation window
questions.prompt: Step 2 of 4. Implement summarize_window(events, start_ms). Events are not guaranteed to be sorted. Include each event whose atMs is greater than or equal to start_ms. Return a fresh dictionary with traffic, errors, and maxLatencyMs keys, where errors counts events whose outcome is "error". Return zero for all fields when the window is empty. Meet O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. When the function returns, the events list and its dictionaries must equal their original values.
constraints: Each event has finite numeric atMs and latencyMs fields plus a string outcome.
Input order is arbitrary and the start boundary is inclusive.
An old event may appear before a later in-window event, so early exit on timestamp is incorrect.
Expected complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; do not sort.
Only the exact outcome string error increments errors.
Return a fresh summary dictionary that does not reuse an input dictionary.
When the function returns, the events list and its dictionaries must equal their original values.

cases.label: keeps scanning after an old event in unsorted input

assertions.label: counts traffic errors and maximum latency

cases.label: returns zeros for an empty window
includes events exactly at the start

questions.title: Apply a per-tenant limit
questions.prompt: Step 3 of 4. Implement admit_per_tenant(jobs, limit). Each job is a dictionary with string id and tenant values. Walk jobs in arrival order and return a fresh list containing the ids of admitted jobs. Admit at most limit jobs for each tenant, while preserving the global order of every job that is admitted. A zero limit admits nothing. Meet O(n) time and O(t) space for n jobs and t tenants. When the function returns, the jobs list and its dictionaries must equal their original values.
constraints: jobs contains JSON-compatible dictionaries with unique string id and tenant values.
limit is a non-negative integer applied independently to each tenant.
Return admitted job ids in their original global arrival order.
Return a fresh result list that does not reuse the jobs list.
Expected complexity: O(n) time and O(t) space for t distinct tenants.
When the function returns, the jobs list and its dictionaries must equal their original values.

assertions.label: admits two jobs per tenant in arrival order

cases.label: admits nothing at a zero limit

assertions.label: admits the first job from each tenant
